negative-call-links-02.scope:
Reject consistent-looking but incorrect RPC owner and operation projections.

Each control changes a complete SDK export and re-runs original-capture wire,
field, contributor, ordered-context and independently derived call-link checks.
Captures and mutated exports must remain outside Git.

rejected.name: reply-operation-owner
rejected.rejection: reply operation name comes from the same original request

rejected.name: request-operation-name
rejected.rejection: precise operation name follows the original UUID/version/opnum

rejected.name: request-interface-alias
rejected.rejection: operation interface follows the original accepted context

rejected.name: request-interface-version
rejected.rejection: operation interface version follows the accepted original proposal

rejected.name: request-operation-number
rejected.rejection: native operation number equals the original request header

rejected.name: reply-context
rejected.rejection: native call context equals the original fixed header

rejected.name: literal-wire-call-id
rejected.rejection: literal native common field Call ID

negative-CLI-publications-01.scope:
Reject mutations of two actual CLI rows under full original PDU mappings.

The full SDK/wire and CLI certificates are mandatory inputs. Controls reuse the
full immutable ID/source mapping but compare two declared row subsets; they do
not pretend to replay a modified whole public capture.

rejected.name: selected-status
rejected.rejection: selected PDU status is the native status

rejected.name: selected-response
rejected.rejection: CLI reply points to the same original request as the SDK

rejected.name: selected-flat-status
rejected.rejection: flat selected aliases equal the owned typed values

negative-publications-01.scope:
Reject missing/forged late publications using a complete owned export.

Require the baseline to contain every decoded nonempty SDK message, then change
one full export per control. Byte ownership, physical rows, aliases and numeric
identities remain independent of the row that published the result.

rejected.name: physical-byte-count
rejected.rejection: ('every original physical fact, label, ordinary PDU and metadata remains exact', 18)

rejected.name: physical-protocol-label
rejected.rejection: ('every original physical fact, label, ordinary PDU and metadata remains exact', 18)

rejected.name: publication-promoted-to-ordinary-contributor
rejected.rejection: ('every original physical fact, label, ordinary PDU and metadata remains exact', 18)

rejected.name: original-byte-owner-replaced-by-publication-frame
rejected.rejection: a current contributor belongs to ordinary PDUs, not the late-publication channel

rejected.name: missing-complete-late-message
rejected.rejection: removing a complete publication cannot pass decoded-message coverage

rejected.name: ordinary-PDU-identity-reused
rejected.rejection: new publications cannot duplicate previously exported ordinary PDUs

explicit_limits: General RPC fragment header/stub reassembly and numeric logical-message ownership remain incomplete.
Multisyntax bind offers, reverse-call ID namespaces, Auth3/SSP verification and NDR service bodies are not newly certified.
SMB named-pipe/tunnel carriers, earlier public source-domain refusals and late pre-origin bytes retain their previous limits.
Derived reorder/drop/snaplen files are controlled observation mutations, not actual socket impairment.
All decoded nonempty SDK IDs are present in these unfiltered exports; this is not equality with all Wireshark fields, support for unrecognized traffic, or a hindsight packet-filter guarantee.
PR remains draft; global TOP30/core protocol conformance is incomplete.
